title: Blind alignment of matched one-dimensional pristine and defect spaces
status_detail: Proposed first follow-on to the human-accepted known-map defect-1D benchmark. No hidden-map alignment experiment is active, calculated, or accepted.
objective: Determine when hidden translation, orbital, spin-frame, and scalar energy-reference maps can be inferred from declared synthetic overlap or anchor data before impurity extraction.
authorized_scope: Plan uniquely identifiable, gauge-equivalent, degenerate, noisy, and incompatible synthetic alignment cases derived from the accepted defect-1D represented spaces.
Declare the overlap, site-anchor, orbital-label, spin-frame, and energy-reference information available to the alignment procedure before evaluation.
Separate alignment-map error, extraction error, model-class residual, spectral error, and wavefunction error, with principal-angle and conditioning diagnostics retained explicitly.
completion_criteria: Recover identifiable hidden maps up to the declared gauge or symmetry equivalence and recover the planted impurity operator within independently established numerical error.

Report non-identifiability, degeneracy, poor conditioning, incompatible rank, incompatible spin space, and incompatible retained subspaces through structured stopping outcomes rather than forced fits.
Retain deterministic synthetic inputs, an independent verifier, figures, provenance, and limitations without a material or scientific-validation claim.
exclusions: No silicon, dopant, DFT, production Wannier, external execution, scientific validation, uncertainty quantification, or public API stabilization is authorized.
The hidden oracle map must not be supplied to the inference action except for post hoc verification.
Map recovery in one synthetic representation does not establish uniqueness or transferability for material calculations.
